name: Thai Beverage Public Company Limited
executive_summary: Thai Beverage Public Company Limited (SGX:Y92) is a diversified ASEAN drinks group—spirits, Chang beer, non-alcoholic beverages, and a controlling stake in Fraser & Neave—trading at roughly 11x earnings with a 5.5% dividend yield and a 14% ROE. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy (13/22 models; composite 80%), driven by cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk factors. The investment case rests on a dominant Thai franchise, recovering beer momentum, and cash-backed distributions at a depressed share price (five-year total return roughly −29%). The central debate is whether low multiples reflect a genuine value opportunity or structural headwinds—spirits volume decline, heavy leverage, negative tangible equity, and persistent discount to intrinsic value despite steady EPS growth. Primary annual regulatory filings are absent from the research pack; interim figures come from news commentary rather than official SGX extracts, limiting forensic depth.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a business that combines scale, recurring demand, and shareholder returns. Y92 passes 13 of 22 value models, including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score (7/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality. Key metrics—P/E 11.4, P/B 1.96, yield 5.5%, ROE 14.3%, FCF ~฿25bn—fit a classic value-and-income profile in consumer defensive.

Business quality supports the screen. ThaiBev is Thailand’s largest beverage company, with spirits (Mekong, SangSom, Chang) as the largest revenue segment, beer and soft drinks providing growth offset, and International Beverage expanding route-to-market in Greater China. H1 FY2026 interim results (per filing-body extract, May 2026) showed revenue of ฿173bn (3% above consensus) and statutory EPS of ฿0.57 (3.6% above expectations), with analysts subsequently lifting full-year EPS forecasts to ฿1.13 (+14% y/y). Beer reportedly regained momentum in the second quarter despite softer half-year group sales.

For a value investor, the hook is a cash-generative franchise priced below its earnings trajectory: EPS has grown at roughly 2–3% annually over five years while the share price fell materially, widening the earnings-yield gap. Dividends appear sustainable—trailing ฿0.62 per share, with payout at ~59% of earnings and ~42% of FCF per secondary commentary in the dividend filing extract—and the screen’s dividend and FCF-yield passes reinforce income appeal. The failed models (Graham Defensive, Net-Net, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Financial Health) flag leverage and intangible-heavy balance sheet rather than operational collapse, which is consistent with a “good business, messy balance sheet” value setup rather than deep distress.
financial_review:
**Filing coverage gap.** The `filings_index.json` catalogue contains zero annual filings (no annual report, 10-K, or equivalent primary extract). One interim item is indexed (May 2026 half-year commentary) plus three “other” items (governance, long-term returns, dividend). All body extracts are third-party news articles (Yahoo Finance / Simply Wall St / Just Drinks), not official SGX or SET regulatory text. No going-concern, contingency, or covenant language from primary filings is available in this pack.

**Interim results (primary filing extract — news commentary, May 2026).** H1 FY2026 revenue: ฿173bn, beating analyst estimates by 3.0%. Statutory EPS: ฿0.57, 3.6% above consensus. Analysts subsequently forecast FY2026 revenue of ฿350.1bn (+6.1% y/y) and EPS of ฿1.13 (+14%), implying acceleration versus historical revenue growth of ~8% p.a. over five years.

**Earlier interim reference (filing extract — Just Drinks, June 2025).** For the six months to end-March (prior reporting period cited in governance coverage): revenue grew 1% to Bt117.62bn; net profit fell 9.2% to Bt17.77bn. Spirits—the largest segment—saw sales down 1.5% to Bt64.52bn (volumes −1.9%) and divisional net profit down 10.3% to Bt11.6bn. Beer and non-alcoholic drinks partially offset weakness.

**Annual trends (fallback: `financials_annual.json` — Yahoo; no primary annual filing available).**

| Metric (฿bn, FY ends Sep) | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 272.4 | 332.9 | 340.3 | 333.3 |
| Net income (common) | 30.1 | 27.4 | 27.2 | 25.4 |
| Diluted EPS (฿) | 1.20 | 1.09 | 1.08 | 1.01 |
| EBITDA | 53.9 | 59.0 | 61.7 | 57.0 |
| Free cash flow | 41.5 | 30.3 | 28.8 | 32.0 |

Revenue expanded sharply from FY2022 (Fraser & Neave consolidation effect) then plateaued; net income and EPS have drifted lower since FY2022 peaks. FY2025 revenue declined 2.1% y/y while net income fell 6.6%, consistent with the spirits softness described in interim commentary.

**Balance sheet and cash flow (Yahoo fallback).** FY2025: total debt ฿235.5bn, net debt ฿184.6bn, cash ฿43.8bn, total assets ฿509.6bn. Goodwill and intangibles total ฿188.5bn, producing negative tangible book value of approximately −฿47.3bn—explaining screen failures on net-net and deep-value criteria. FY2025 operating cash flow was ฿46.0bn against capex of ฿14.1bn; dividends paid ฿15.6bn, comfortably covered by FCF of ฿32.0bn. Interest expense rose to ฿8.5bn (FY2025) from ฿6.2bn (FY2022), reflecting higher leverage post F&N acquisition.

**Quarterly bridge (Yahoo fallback).** Most recent half-year quarters show revenue of ฿85.4bn (prior year quarter) and ฿86.5bn (current), with EPS rising from ฿0.27 to ฿0.29—consistent with the reported H1 ฿173bn / ฿0.57 interim figures and suggesting modest H1 FY2026 improvement versus prior year.

**Historical annual reference (filing extract — Just Drinks).** FY2023/24 (to 30 September): revenue Bt340.29bn (+2.2%); net profit Bt35.27bn (+0.6%). This broadly aligns with Yahoo FY2024 figures, lending cross-check comfort on order of magnitude.
risks_and_flags:
**Governance and control.** The Sirivadhanabhakdi family controls ~66% via holding companies. SGX-lodged documents (June 2025 filing extract) show stakes transferred to five children while Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi, aged 81, retains authority to “manage and make all decisions in respect of the business and assets” of the group. Concentrated control creates related-party, capital-allocation, and succession uncertainty not captured by quantitative screens.

**Leverage and balance-sheet quality.** Net debt of ~฿185bn and negative tangible equity are material. The screen failed Financial Health and net-net models. Rising interest expense (฿8.5bn FY2025) absorbs a growing share of operating profit. No covenant or going-concern disclosures are available in this pack’s filing bodies.

**Spirits cyclicality and mix.** Spirits remain the largest segment and showed volume and profit decline in the prior interim period. A sustained spirits slowdown would pressure group margins despite beer recovery.

**Portfolio complexity and capital deployment.** The 2024 Fraser & Neave stake increase to 69.61% (share-swap) adds listed-associate exposure and balance-sheet intangibles. M&A history (Asiaeuro International Beverage acquisition, January 2025) adds integration and China route-to-market execution risk.

**Market dislocation.** Five-year total shareholder return of approximately −29% (January 2026 filing extract) despite positive EPS growth suggests the market assigns a persistent conglomerate discount, Thai macro/political risk, or concerns over capital structure—any of which could keep multiples depressed.

**Dividend sustainability flags.** Secondary commentary (May 2026 dividend extract) notes payout at 59% of earnings and flat dividends over ten years, implying limited growth rather than imminent cut—but also limited reinvestment signal. Screen failed High Dividend Yield (threshold not met at current classification).

**Data quality.** Absence of primary annual and interim regulatory extracts is itself a red flag for verify-before-trade: key figures rely on Yahoo and news aggregation rather than audited filing text.

research_rationale: Improving H1 profitability, attractive multiples, and robust FCF/dividend metrics support the quantitative strong-buy signal, but absent primary annual filings, elevated leverage, spirits softness, and family-control overhang prevent full confirmation.
